An octopus has three hearts and blue blood.

Two hearts pump blood to the gills; the third moves it around the rest of the body, and it stops whenever the animal swims. That is why an octopus would rather walk along the seabed: swimming costs it a heart.

In 1492, while three caravels were crossing the Atlantic, the octopuses of the Mediterranean had already spent 300 million years solving problems with their arms. Each arm thinks a little for itself: two thirds of its neurons are not in the head.

They open jars, remember faces and, it seems, dream. They sleep with their skin changing colour, as if going over the day.

Dear Grandma,

I am writing from the kitchen, which smells just like yours when it rains. I have put the radio on low and closed my eyes for a while, the way you did on Sunday afternoons.

You asked when I am coming back. On 23 December, on the 5:40 pm train. I have the book you lent me; I am on chapter XII, the one with the lighthouse. You were right: it is better than it looked.

Save me a slice of the apple pie. And do not scold me for my handwriting: a parrot is reading you this letter.

A big kiss.

A recipe for one large loaf.

Ingredients: 500 g of strong flour, 350 ml of lukewarm water, 10 g of salt and 3 g of dried yeast.

Mix the flour with the salt. Dissolve the yeast in the water and add it little by little, stirring by hand until no loose flour is left. There is no need to knead much: just fold the dough over itself four times, once every half hour.

Leave it covered to rest overnight, about 12 hours. In the morning, shape it into a ball, score it with a knife and bake it at 230 °C for 45 minutes, with a bowl of water inside the oven.

Wait for it to cool before cutting. That crackle is the reward.
